subject: Operational runbook: evidence gates & onboarding for GRCFlow integration
messages:
From: GRCFlow Integrations <partners@grcflow.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence exchange proposal + sample mappings

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro via the partner portal. GRCFlow builds a lightweight evidence gateway that connects customer GRC consoles to vendor evidence endpoints — we think Redwood's private deployments would benefit from a direct connector to automate SOC2 evidence pulls and pen-test attestation uploads.

Attached is a short spec that shows our expected evidence schemas and an initial mapping for common Redwood artifacts (audit logs, config snapshots, build artifacts). High-level asks:
- Can Redwood accept signed evidence bundles via S3 presigned uploads?
- Do you support a webhook acknowledgement for each evidence bundle ingest?
- What retention/access controls would you require for third-party evidence?

Would you and your security contact be available for a 45-minute tech onboarding next week? We can bring our connector engineer and a product manager.

Attachment: GRCFlow-Evidence-Spec-v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Sanjay Kumar
Head of Integrations, GRCFlow
partners@grcflow.com
+1 (415) 555-0246

P.S. We also work with a pen-test partner (PenTestWorks) for bundled attestation deliveries — happy to loop them in if useful.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: GRCFlow Integrations <partners@grcflow.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence exchange proposal + sample mappings

Thanks Sanjay — appreciate the spec and the clear mapping. Looping in our security leads (Soojin and Mina) and the infra engineer who owns the private connector work.

Quick answers up front:
- Presigned S3 uploads are supported for partner-sourced artifacts, but we require signed manifests and an HMAC envelope for every bundle to validate origin.
- We can publish webhook acks; our ingestion pipeline emits event ids and an ingest status callback (success/fail/validation_error).
- Retention: by default third-party evidence is stored for 365 days in a segregated bucket; we can offer extended retention on contract. Access is RBAC-controlled and gated by the customer’s org admin.

Next steps I propose:
1) Security scoping call (45 min) — Soojin, Mina: can we do Wed 11/4 at 10am PT?
2) Tech onboarding (connector walk-through) — include GRCFlow engineer + our infra owner.
3) Draft an operational runbook (who uploads what, names of webhooks, failure/retry behavior, SLOs).

Also, Sanjay: please send sample signed manifests (JSON) and the exact header format you use for HMAC so we can validate during the onboarding.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Partner Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.inference

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence exchange proposal + sample mappings

Thanks — I reviewed the spec and have a short checklist before we commit to production data flows:

Security checklist (initial):
- Mutual TLS for admin APIs or signed JWTs for partner service accounts.
- Signed manifest with SHA256 checksums for every artifact.
- Proof of chain-of-custody (timestamped signature + uploader identity).
- Ingest validation rules: schema mismatch = reject (400) + webhook callback.
- Audit log requirements: we need per-bundle ingest logs forwarded to our audit sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) with retention as per the customer's policy.
- Pen-test attestation handling: separate namespace + limited-time access tokens for reviewers.

Operational questions:
- What are your recommended retry windows for transient failures? We typically allow exponential backoff up to 6 retries and then open an incident.
- Do you support bundle-level encryption keys (customer KMS) or do you require partner KMS?

If we agree on the above, we'll draft the runbook sections for: upload flow, webhook contract, error modes, and SOC2 evidence tagging conventions.

Sanjay — can you confirm GRCFlow supports signed manifests and whether you can rotate keys on a per-customer basis? Also, please share any sample bundles (sanitized) so we can run validation against our pipeline.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
